sample_plan.subpopulation_description: U.S. residents aged 0–2, including infants and very young children whose daily needs and activities are shaped by caregivers. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
U.S. residents aged 3–14, including school-age children and young teenagers whose activities may be shaped by caregivers and developmental stage. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 3–14, including children and young teenagers; independent hobbies and adult behaviors are left unconstrained for this broad developmental band. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

A U.S. resident aged 15–24 who participates in the labor force and has had little or interrupted access to formal schooling. This age range includes older adolescents and young adults; eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
U.S. residents aged 15–24 who participate in the labor force, spanning older adolescents and young adults. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
U.S. residents aged 15–24 who are not currently participating in the labor force, including older adolescents and young adults. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 who are employed and participate in the labor force; this directive includes a progressive political-belief contrast while retaining the supplied demographic option sets. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 who are employed and participate in the labor force, with a contrast in optimism, food preferences, shopping, health, product attitudes, and travel. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
U.S. residents aged 25–54 who are employed and participate in the labor force, with varied cultural influences and everyday habits. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

A U.S. resident aged 25–54 who participates in the labor force, is employed in a specialist-compatible occupation, and has a highly accomplished advanced-learning profile. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

A U.S. resident aged 25–54 who participates in the labor force, is employed in a specialist-compatible occupation, and has exceptionally broad intellectual curiosity and advanced expertise. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
A U.S. resident aged 25–54 who participates in the labor force, is unemployed, and is actively seeking work. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 25–54 who are not currently participating in the labor force. This group allows for varied routines and life circumstances without prescribing a cause for nonparticipation. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
U.S. residents aged 55–64 who are employed and participate in the labor force, with varied household and lifestyle circumstances. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 55–64 who are not currently participating in the labor force. The directive includes a strongly negative attitude contrast without restricting the supplied demographic options. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

A U.S. resident aged 65 or older who participates in the labor force and is employed. The age range includes older adults with varied health and support needs. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 65 or older who are not currently participating in the labor force. This group retains the supplied income, race, gender, region, and settlement option sets while including a shopping-extreme contrast. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.

U.S. residents aged 65 or older who are not currently participating in the labor force. The directive includes a novelty-seeking product-attitude contrast while leaving demographic marginals open. Eligibility does not depend on citizenship.
